properties.description:
Run one server, attach one design, read resident memory. Attach a SECOND design and read it again. The delta is the per-open-store cost; the intercept is the per-process cost. One process with one store gives one point and cannot separate them.

Reproduce the reading with: grep -E '^(VmRSS|VmHWM)' /proc/$(pgrep -f 'reflow2-mcp.*serve-shared')/status

WHY THIS PARTICULAR MEASUREMENT: it is the single split that decides one-service-many-graphs against process-per-project. dec:one-process-many-stores was accepted CONDITIONALLY on 2026-08-06 and its own risk list says "N open graphs is N block caches and N tantivy indices, and without a cap a busy server degrades in a way that looks like reflow2 being slow" — that risk has never been quantified. Every capacity claim on flo2's side is currently arithmetic over this unknown.

Requested by @ajs from flo2's 2026-09-13 session.
properties.findings:
Re-measured 2026-09-27 with the method now executable (tools/measure_open_design_memory.py), on 4 copies of reflow2's own design (5,616 nodes) with MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=2:
- intercept about 16 MB;
- about 36 MB per open design, nearly all private heap (RssAnon 35.7, RssFile 0.7), taken at open.
The 2026-09-13 slope of ~5 MB was on small designs. See fact:a-reflow2-sized-open-design-costs-about-36mb-of-heap-and-rocksdb-is-not-most-of-it-2026-09-27.
properties.name: The per-open-design memory cost is measured, separating per-process from per-store
